onboarding_headline: Read what's there, and notice what isn't.
onboarding_blurb: A quiet news reader: what your sources actually sent you, and — just as plainly — what they left out. The lens flags loaded language, and with a dictionary downloaded it defines any word on a long-press. Everything runs on your phone by default.
onboarding_mode_explainer: Controls shown keeps an obvious back button and the utility bar. Immersive hides them for a bare page; swipe right to go back. You can change this any time in Settings.
tour_loom_body: What your sources actually sent you, woven against what you actually read. Pull down on your stand, or tap the coloured bar above the stories.
tour_flash_body: The day's headlines cut to a line each, with a way back into the full piece. Off until you switch it on, in Settings.
tour_cast_body: An article read aloud in a voice that runs on your phone rather than a server. Also in Settings; it asks before downloading anything.
tour_clippings_body: Tap the bookmark while reading to keep a piece. Clippings holds them as torn scraps of the paper.
tour_history_body: A short dated column above the day's stories, from Wikipedia's own “on this day”. Off until you switch it on.
tour_footer: Nothing here reaches for anything you didn't ask for. The three switches above stay off until you turn them on.
language_explainer: Nooz's own text. Stories always stay in the language their publisher wrote them in.
list_nothing_unread_body: Every story in this list has been opened. Pinch out, or tap here, to see the whole list again.
list_showing_unread_only: Showing unread only, tap to show every story
list_showing_all: Showing every story, tap to show unread only
reader_full_story: Read the full story at the source ↗
loom_use_actions: Use actions for a single stream's counts.
loom_nothing_flowed: Nothing flowed from your %1$s this day.
globe_nothing_flowed: Nothing has flowed from here yet.
globe_mix: %1$d stories: %2$s. Use actions to spin or change the band.
loom_empty: Nothing flowed this day. The loom weaves once your sources do.
loom_no_archive: Most sources are live RSS/Atom feeds with no way to ask for a past date; this shows what they’re serving right now, not an archive.
contrast_no_reads: No reads yet today. The map fills in as you read.
cross_what_changed: What changed since the previous period
cross_no_earlier: No earlier period yet to compare against.
stand_subtitle: Browse the papers. Pick a pile to read that slice.
stand_no_full_text: The full text is not in this feed. Open the story to read it at the source.
stand_no_full_text_yet: The full text is not in this feed yet. Open the story to read it at the source.
reader_no_text: This source’s feed didn’t include the article text. Read the full piece at the source below.
reader_no_link: This item’s feed didn’t include a usable link back to its source.
loom_subtitle: What flowed from your sources, woven against what you actually read.
loom_strip_open: Open the Loom — what flowed, woven against what you read
loom_nothing_read_yet: You haven’t read anything yet — the strip fills in as you open stories.
clippings_empty_body: Tap the clip icon on any item to save it here — it stays even if you later remove or disable its source.
sources_starters_body: A short list of pre-checked, currently-live feeds — switch on any you like.
edit_source_failing: This source is failing to fetch
edit_pick_a_feed: This page declares more than one feed, pick one:
edit_paste_hint: Paste a feed or a site URL — the app finds the feed; fetches only what you add.
edit_globe_hint: Drag to spin · pinch to widen · ring shows the band’s topic mix
edit_catalogue_hint: Optionally point this at a catalogue.json to refresh starters and free-tier limits without an app update. Nothing is fetched unless you tap refresh; there is no default URL, since this build can’t verify one is live.
settings_theme_follow: Follow the phone’s light or dark setting
settings_while_you_read_body: Every so often, a real line pulled from something you’ve already read.
settings_today_in_history_body: A few dated lines above the day’s stories, from Wikipedia’s own “On this day” selection. This is the one thing Nooz fetches from outside the sources you added, so it stays off until you turn it on.
settings_highlight_loaded_body: Underlines charged wording as you read; tap it for the evidence.
settings_immersive_body: Hides the back button and controls for a bare page. Off by default; swipe right or tap back to return.
settings_more_body: Dictionary, reader intelligence and models, gestures, your data, about.
settings_dictionary_body: Download a dictionary, then long-press any word as you read for its meaning, Kindle-style.
settings_crash_body: The report stayed on your device; nothing was sent anywhere.
settings_flash_body: Today’s news compressed to 10 words or fewer. Runs on your device once you download a model below, or through your own key.
settings_cast_body: The full article read aloud in a natural on-device voice, never the robotic system reader. Its own model, downloaded separately from Flash’s.
settings_whats_inside_body: The Loom, Flash, Cast, Clippings — and where each one lives.
settings_gestures_body: Two-finger reader gestures. Defaults are on.
settings_word_list_body: Turn off individual default flags, or add your own words to watch for.
settings_your_data_body: Export everything as open JSON: preferences, your region and topics, your sources, your clippings, and the coarse read log. Local only; API keys are never included.
settings_about_body: Nooz is a news reader whose subject is omission: what got left out. It’s made by mdhv.xyz, a small studio of focused, quiet apps.
settings_translation_body: One language pair at a time. Downloaded once, then it works offline — what you look up is never sent anywhere.
settings_no_indic_pair: No Indian-language pair is available from this source yet.
flash_coming_soon: Coming soon: today's news compressed to 10 words or fewer, once on-device intelligence is ready.
flash_tap_to_compress: Tap to compress today's news to 10 words or fewer
flash_setup_link: Set up an on-device model or connect an API →
cast_tap_to_hear: Tap to hear this article read aloud in a natural voice
cast_setup_link: Set up an on-device narration model →
history_try_again: Try loading Today in History again
cross_section_explainer: your %1$s share of what you read ÷ its share of the stream; above 1x means you read more of this topic than it made up of the stream
loom_ask_gdelt_again: Ask GDELT again for this day
loom_fetch_gdelt: Fetch GDELT results for this day
lens_no_definition: No definition for this word in your dictionary.
defuse_needs_setup: No neutral rewrite yet. This needs an on-device model or your own key, from Settings › Reader intelligence.
word_list_body: Words and phrases the reading lens underlines as loaded language or editorial hedging. Turn off any default you don't want flagged, or add your own below.
model_on_device_body: Nooz tries your device first, automatically: nothing to set up. Download a model below and it runs right on your device; until then (or unless you add a key below), the lens honestly reports "unavailable" instead of guessing.
model_download_body: Real, open-source models verified by this app's own catalogue. Download them here: they won't run automatically (see On-device), but once downloaded they're on disk and ready.
model_local_unavailable: On this computer Nooz uses a key you supply. Running a model on the device itself arrives in a later version.
model_byok_body: Route defuse rewrites to your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Results are always marked cloud; your key stays on this device.
